text:
alex-cust: FYI p95 token latency jumped from ~70ms -> 700-1.1s starting ~2026-03-17T03:18Z on dedicated-eu2-pool-58. Also saw ~5% 429s with 'server overloaded' on short window. sample=req-64b2f

mika-support: thx — we're looking. tenant id + model + any recent deploys?

alex-cust: tenant=luminate-prod-404, model=rwd-open-7b-q5, no deploys in last 48h. traffic had a short burst at 03:16-03:20 (~2.8x concurrency). autoscaler did a +3 scale at 03:17.

infra-bot: autoscaler: pool=dedicated-eu2-pool-58 scaled +3 at 2026-03-17T03:17:04Z (reason=surge_detected, scale_op_id=scale-9911)

jamal-sre: can we repro with a controlled generator? @sofia-runtime pull node/MIG mapping for the hot period. if sibling SMs spiked it's likely co-residency.

sofia-runtime: inventory snapshot (03:15-03:22): node=gpunode-58, physical_gpu=ampere-3, MIG slices:
```
slice_id  owner_tenant           mig_profile
4601      luminate-prod-404     1g.5gb
4603      atlas-batch-7         1g.5gb
4607      system-monitor        1g.5gb
```
SM util (12s samples) -> baseline 28% then spike to 96% for ~55s at 03:17:40. dram_bw peaked ~82%.

sofia-runtime: perf counters show higher 'atomic' and 'shared_mem_stall' from slice 4603 during spike window — consistent with heavy sampling/beam loops from atlas-batch-7.

alex-cust: our traces show step-time increased at 03:17:35 for req-64b2f. saw 4x slower token emission for several steps.

jamal-sre: runtime drops 429s when request queue exceeds limit. root cause seems sibling SM saturation. mitigation options: (1) immediate eviction of noisy slice, (2) change packer to prefer isolation over fractional fill for nodes with historical sm spikes, (3) soft knobs — throttle batch sizes or sample settings at tenant side.

mika-support: customer requests immediate relief. can we evict atlas-batch-7 from gpunode-58?

oncall-sre: we can drain node/gpunode-58 and trigger allocation remap. eviction will briefly bump reschedules — need explicit go.

alex-cust: please proceed, it's affecting production.

infra-bot: eviction_request: initiated_by=jamal-sre target_node=gpunode-58 at 2026-03-17T03:28:12Z evicting_allocations=[4603]

jamal-sre: plan: 1) drain gpunode-58 2) packer remaps luminate slice to different node 3) run small parallel load (script below) 4) validate p95 and sm metrics.

jamal-sre: load test (run from infra worker):
```
# quick stress, parallel clients
import requests,concurrent.futures, time
URL='https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
H={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED'}
def call():
  return requests.post(URL,json={'model':'rwd-open-7b-q5','input':'test'},timeout=30).status_code
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
  start=time.time()
  res=list(ex.map(lambda _: call(), range(600)))
  print('done',res.count(200),res.count(429))
```

sofia-runtime: placement excerpt for scale-9911:
```
[placement] scale_event=scale-9911 candidates=[gpunode-58,gpunode-61]
score(gpunode-58)=0.91 (fractional pack allowed, warm-kv benefit)
score(gpunode-61)=0.72
chosen=gpunode-58
reason=warmed cache + lower predicted cold-latency
```

sofia-runtime: heuristic favored warm cache which kept atlas-batch-7 co-resident. we'll propose change: if node.sm_history.p95 > 75% prefer isolation.

oncall-sre: draining gpunode-58 now, remap in progress. expect ~3-5m for reallocations.

infra-bot: allocation_remap: alloc=4601 owner=luminate-prod-404 from_node=gpunode-58 -> to_node=gpunode-73 at 2026-03-17T03:32:09Z

jamal-sre: running load test after remap.

jamal-sre: quick results: p95 down to ~110ms, 429s ~0.5%. target node (gpunode-73) SM util ~36% steady. dram_bw stable.

alex-cust: latency returned to expected levels — thanks. will monitor.

mika-support: filing SUP-2026-4839: followups: (a) audit autoscaler placement heuristics when fractional packing chosen, (b) add alert when fractional_pack && sm_p95>70%, (c) discuss tenant isolation premium option.

jamal-sre: leaving eviction active for 12h, monitoring. reopen if recurrence. will escalate to scheduler if we see repeated co-residency with noisy tenants.

alex-cust: appreciate the quick response :thumbsup:"
